include: The Social Vibecoding React platform shell
Platform-owned routes and reusable shell patterns
The shell-side hosted-app frame and compatibility adapters
exclude: Child-app source code and visual identity

maturity.candidate: Available for shell migration work; contract changes require catalog and evidence updates.
maturity.stable: Approved for broad shell reuse; breaking changes require migration notes.
maturity.deprecated: Existing uses may remain temporarily; no new uses are allowed.

contract: Use semantic elements and accessible names for every interactive control.
Support keyboard operation and visible focus wherever the pattern is interactive.
Keep serious and critical Storybook accessibility violations at zero.
accessibility.evidence: Named Storybook states plus the Storybook accessibility test gate.

dataBoundary.contract: Presentation receives typed props or calls an owned @/lib adapter; direct endpoints and platform globals are forbidden.
ActionLink and ActionAnchor receive destinations, labels, visual variants, and navigation policy from callers. They own no route data, authorization, or external-destination policy.

contract: ActionLink and ActionAnchor always render semantic anchors, never buttons.
Disabled links expose aria-disabled, leave keyboard order, and guard activation.
Visible focus and disabled treatment match the shared action visual authority.
accessibility.evidence: ActionLink internal, external, primary, outline, and disabled Storybook states plus the source-derived navigation ledger.

dataBoundary.contract: The definition-list Metric receives one label, one value, and optional numeric presentation from its caller. It owns no fetching, formatting, domain terminology, or collection layout.

contract: Metric renders exactly one semantic term and description pair for use inside a definition list.
Numeric values use tabular numerals without changing their spoken value.
The caller owns the surrounding definition list and its accessible section context.
accessibility.evidence: Metric Default, Numeric, and LongValue Storybook states plus the styled Storybook accessibility gate.

dataBoundary.contract: StreamRow receives a typed destination, visible content, optional read emphasis, a stable caller-owned anchor, optional quiet trailing value, and at most one caller-owned sibling action. It owns no fetching, mutation, authorization, or domain routing.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: A stream may contain cursor-paged records and receive live updates while each row renders one destination and at most one sibling action.

performance.mountPolicy: Preserve the row and its content anchor while read state changes; remove the unread action without shifting the left anatomy.
sensitiveInteractions: Mark one row read without navigating or rebuilding unrelated rows.
Preserve destination-first keyboard order and non-overlapping pointer targets.

contract: The row destination is one semantic Link with a specific accessible name.
The optional secondary action is a sibling, never nested inside the Link.
Destination precedes the secondary action in keyboard order and both show visible focus.
Coarse-pointer targets provide at least 48 by 48 CSS-pixel reach without overlap.
accessibility.evidence: StreamRow read/unread, comparable-record, mobile, dark, and long-content stories plus Activity, Work, Home-attention, and Leaderboard browser tests for semantics, focus, navigation, mutation, read-only behavior, and geometry.

dataBoundary.contract: The icon receives a Lucide icon object, canonical size and accessible labelling props; it owns no application data.

contract: Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
Standalone semantic icons require an aria-label.
All platform glyphs use the canonical icon size grid.
accessibility.evidence: PlatformIcon Storybook states and component tests.

dataBoundary.contract: ThemeSwitcherView is props-only; ThemeSwitcher owns persistence exclusively through @/lib/theme.

contract: Expose one mutually exclusive light/dark/system preference choice set.
Communicate the selected mode programmatically.
Retain keyboard operation supplied by the official ToggleGroup.
accessibility.evidence: LightSelected, DarkSelected and SystemSelected Storybook states plus route tests proving stored preference behavior and System semantic-token parity with explicit Light/Dark.

dataBoundary.contract: AppIdentity receives immutable app id/slug, display name and optional image. It derives its v1 finite palette slot locally and owns no route data or persistence.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: AppIdentity can repeat across a discovery collection, but the identity itself renders one image or one monogram and owns no collection.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep each identity mounted with its owning app row or card; collection virtualization remains the route's responsibility.
sensitiveInteractions: Remote artwork failure must fall back without changing the surrounding app layout.

contract: Fallback artwork and supplied app images are decorative because the adjacent app name is the accessible label.
Identity foreground, border and surrounding focus treatment meet the semantic-token contrast matrix in both modes.
Forced-colors mode preserves a visible artwork boundary and fallback glyph.
accessibility.evidence: AppIdentity Storybook states, deterministic mapping tests, semantic token contrast checks, and forced-colors browser evidence.

dataBoundary.contract: StatusDot receives a non-empty subject, finite semantic role, and human state label. Explicit App, Node, Connection, and Service adapters map raw domain values; raw API strings never choose colors.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: StatusDot may repeat in app, notification, or operational lists while each instance renders one compact state.

performance.mountPolicy: Preserve the status node while its adapter-fed state changes so live updates do not rebuild the surrounding row.
sensitiveInteractions: A live state change updates only the dot and its text or accessible name.

contract: Color is never the only status signal; visible labels or an accessible dot label are required.
StatusDot owns the '<subject>, <state>' accessible phrase.
Dot-only status is exposed as a named image to assistive technology.
Forced-colors mode preserves a visible non-color state boundary.
accessibility.evidence: StatusDot role and App/Node/Connection/Service adapter stories, semantic token contrast checks, and forced-colors browser evidence.

dataBoundary.contract: TopBar receives the screen name, an optional Back callback, and caller-owned contextual actions. It reads only the shell attention count for its menu dot, and performs no routing, fetching, authorization, bridge or iframe work.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: Exactly one TopBar accompanies every screen; it is the shell's only route chrome.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep the TopBar and the adjacent hosted app mounted while title, attention, authorization and contextual actions update.
sensitiveInteractions: Title or action changes must not resize, reload or remount the hosted iframe.
Exactly one reciprocal Use or Improve action remains reachable as authorization changes.

contract: The TopBar renders the screen's sole h1, whether that name is a platform destination or a dApp context.
Menu, Back, Close and overflow controls have specific accessible names and 48 CSS-pixel targets.
The platform menu shows an attention dot, never a count, and the dot is understandable without color.
At narrow-mobile width, application identity or the platform page name remains complete while caller-owned utilities move to a secondary row and Back remains available.
Use and Improve are never presented as permanent equal-weight modes.
accessibility.evidence: Default, attention, action, icon-action, nested-back, long-title, mobile and dark stories render both themes with interaction assertions; TopBar and AppTopBar narrow stories prove complete identity above reachable utilities, and route contracts prove one bar and one h1 per screen.

dataBoundary.contract: PlatformNavigation receives visible route items, route matchers, Activity attention evidence, Node status evidence and authorization decisions from shell adapters. It fetches no platform state.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: The accepted platform information architecture has five primary destinations, one Node row and a bounded utility footer.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep navigation and the adjacent focused app mounted while Activity counts, Node state, authorization, active route and drawer state update.
sensitiveInteractions: Opening and closing the narrow drawer must not remount the hosted iframe.
Activity and Node evidence updates must not rebuild unrelated route content.

contract: Expose one navigation landmark named Platform navigation.
Only the matching destination owns aria-current; the dApps brand link is not a second current item.
The narrow drawer closes with Escape and returns focus to its trigger.
Node state and Activity attention retain non-color accessible evidence.
accessibility.evidence: Desktop, narrow open/closed, active route, utility footer, authorization, attention, Node and dark-theme Storybook states; browser integration later proves focus return and iframe continuity.

dataBoundary.contract: When mounted by an approved host composition, PlatformBottomNavigation receives exactly three canonical mobile destinations and the current pathname through props. PlatformShell does not currently mount it. It fetches no route, authorization, attention, or platform state.

contract: Expose one mobile-only navigation landmark named Mobile primary navigation.
Render exactly three visible links named Home, Work and Search in that order.
Only the matching destination owns aria-current, and Search preserves the existing Explore route.
Each link has non-overlapping 48 CSS-pixel reach for coarse pointers.
When enabled, the persistent Overlay stays outside and does not geometrically overlap Paper; the route scroll owner remains inside Paper and the Overlay clears the active device safe area.
The production shell does not mount this candidate until a separate product acceptance reopens its integration.
accessibility.evidence: Home, Work, Search and dark Storybook states preserve the isolated component contract. The production-shell browser contract proves the candidate is absent at mobile and desktop widths.

dataBoundary.contract: HomeAppShortcut receives one AppRecord, a direct-launch destination, finite presentation status and optional reorder callbacks. Grouping, ordering, persistence, rollback and navigation remain route responsibilities.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: Home intentionally exposes a sparse set of pinned or recent personal shortcuts rather than the complete app catalog.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep each shortcut and its focused reorder control mounted across optimistic earlier/later updates.
sensitiveInteractions: An optimistic reorder retains keyboard focus and rolls back through the route adapter without rebuilding unrelated shortcuts.

contract: The direct-launch action includes the dApp name.
Status has a visible label and a '<subject>, <state>' accessible name.
Earlier/later controls have dApp-specific labels and truthful disabled states.
AppIdentity remains decorative because the adjacent dApp name labels the destination.
accessibility.evidence: Running, unavailable, collaborator and every reorder-edge Storybook state render both themes and interaction assertions.

dataBoundary.contract: ExploreAppCard receives one AppRecord, a details destination, finite presentation status and optional community signal. Search, filtering, categories, pagination and app actions remain route or details responsibilities.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: Explore renders the searchable catalog in a responsive grid; the route may page or virtualize if production size later exceeds the initial bounded collection.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep each visible card mounted while status or community evidence updates; collection filtering remains the route's responsibility.
sensitiveInteractions: Updating one card's status must not rebuild or resize unrelated cards in the catalog grid.

contract: The sole details action includes the dApp name.
The card has no hidden overflow or management action.
Missing descriptions omit the description region instead of inventing filler.
AppIdentity remains decorative because the adjacent dApp name labels the card.
accessibility.evidence: Running, Building, AwaitingSecrets, Unavailable, WithCommunity and NoDescription stories render both themes with assertions.

dataBoundary.contract: FocusedAppFrame receives one loaded AppDetail, validated route path input, current iframe token, offline state and callbacks. The route adapter owns API calls, token refresh cadence, online subscriptions, retry policy, native title sync and routing.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: The focused shell hosts at most one active child-app iframe.

performance.mountPolicy: The iframe must stay mounted across drawer open/close, chrome/status updates, Activity/Node evidence updates and temporary shell focus changes. Only a deliberate URL, token or retry transition may replace it.
sensitiveInteractions: Translate or inert the focused-app plane for narrow navigation without remounting the iframe.
Preserve iframe form, scroll, JavaScript and focus state across shell updates.
Refresh credentials without silently changing sandbox, allow or direct-link path semantics.

contract: The iframe has the dApp name as its title.
Loading is announced politely without a fake ready frame.
Offline and unavailable states use named alerts with a visible recovery action where recovery is possible.
Focus and inert behavior are proven later in the real browser host fixture, not simulated in Storybook.
accessibility.evidence: TokenUnavailable, OfflineRetry, UnsafeDestination, SelfHosted and NotRunning Storybook states plus the required Wave 6 browser host-contract matrix.

dataBoundary.contract: HostedAppStage receives platform chrome, one route-owned state, optional staged-review treatment and child content. It owns no fetching, iframe permissions, routing, history, console registration or native bridge behavior.

contract: The hosted-app wrapper preserves its caller-owned single level-one heading and keyboard order.
The persistent card contains loading, error and ready content without moving route chrome.
Staged review keeps its status label and information surface legible in both themes.
The wrapper does not repaint platform navigation, add interactive controls or duplicate labels owned by route chrome.
accessibility.evidence: Eight HostedAppStage Storybook matrix states render paired light and dark fixtures, plus focused-host and staging-preview browser contracts.

dataBoundary.contract: Message history, connection state and callbacks arrive as props; MessageScroller owns scroll behavior.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: A long-running Dev session can accumulate an open-ended transcript even when history is loaded incrementally.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep the transcript scroller mounted while tokens stream, connection state changes, and the composer updates.
sensitiveInteractions: Append streaming content without rerendering unrelated shell regions.
Preserve scroll anchoring and jump-to-latest behavior as history grows.

dataBoundary.contract: Board records and mutation callbacks arrive through the dev-board adapter; the board does not call endpoints directly.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: Active issues, reviews, and completed history can create long columns even though the adapter pages older work.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep board columns and the active card mounted across filtering, view changes, and supported reorder operations.
sensitiveInteractions: Filter the visible work set without blocking input.
Drag and reorder supported cards while preserving pointer feedback and column state.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: General and scoped discussions grow continuously and retain paged history.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep the transcript mounted while socket state, reactions, replies, edits, and composer state change.
sensitiveInteractions: Append or reconcile live messages without resetting scroll position.
Update reactions and authored edits without rebuilding unrelated message rows.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: The administration surface can contain the complete platform user set and filters it interactively.

performance.mountPolicy: Preserve search focus and the current filtered result set while individual user records update.
sensitiveInteractions: Filter a large user set on each search change.
Update one user record without rebuilding unaffected rows.

expectedCollectionSize.rationale: The visible feed is cursor-paged but live events may refresh and deduplicate the first page.

performance.mountPolicy: Keep loaded pages and the active notification mounted while live events refresh the authoritative first page.
sensitiveInteractions: Prepend and deduplicate live notifications without discarding older pages.
Mark one or all visible notifications read without rebuilding unrelated shell regions.
